name: Yttrium
occurrence: Found alongside rare-earth elements in minerals like xenotime, though chemically it behaves like a lanthanide despite sitting in the d-block.
majorUses: Red phosphor in older CRT and LED displays
notableCharacteristics: Named after Ytterby, a Swedish village that lends its name to no fewer than four elements (yttrium, ytterbium, terbium, and erbium).
whyHere: Its single 4d electron and similar ionic size to the lanthanides means it's chemically grouped with rare-earth elements in practice, even though it sits in the d-block by strict electron configuration.
didYouKnow: The tiny Swedish village of Ytterby has an entire mine that gave its name to four different elements — yttrium, ytterbium, terbium, and erbium — an unmatched record for any single location.
genZNote: One village, four elements named after it. Ytterby really said 'we're the periodic table's hometown now.'
